result.title: LeafSkill: Efficient Leaf-Level Action Grounding for Recursive LLM Agents
result.summary: Recursive large language model (LLM) agents solve long-horizon tasks through decomposition, execution, and environmental feedback. Yet after producing an atomic subtask, they often invoke the same large model again to translate a familiar instruction into an executable action. We observe that high-level planning is task-specific, whereas leaf-level action grounding recurs across tasks and can be checked against environment-admitted actions. We introduce LeafSkill, an external reuse layer that retrieves semantically related grounding experience, binds action templates to current objects and admissible actions, and uses a lightweight 1.7B selector to choose a bound action or defer the unchanged subtask to the original agent. Skills remain outside the model parameters, allowing a frozen selector to use post-training additions. Under lexical and syntactic paraphrases, exact matching retrieves none of the reference actions, while semantic retrieval preserves 96.0% and 97.0% candidate coverage; the frozen selector adopts 97.34% of unseen skill types. On an independent confirmation set of 200 Robotouille tasks, LeafSkill completes 137 tasks versus 121 for ReCAP (68.5% vs. 60.5%, exact McNemar p=.0259). On the 106 tasks completed by both, it reduces Qwen3.5-27B tokens by 14.42% and calls by 14.08%. A separate held-out repeat yields a consistent 9.0-point success gain and 18.98% token reduction. Reusable leaf grounding can thus improve task completion while reducing host-model inference without replacing high-level planning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LeafSkill：在模型参数外复用叶级动作接地经验，语义检索后绑定动作模板与当前可行动作，并由 1.7B 选择器决定采用或退回原 agent；在 Robotouille 上提升成功率并减少宿主模型 token 与调用。
AI.relevance_reason: 不涉及视觉或 latent 推理；其外部技能复用与「采用/延迟」选择器可能为 LVR 的推理状态缓存、计算复用及停止或委派决策提供可核查的类比线索。
